title: Collections That Hunt the Payer, Not the Patient
one_liner: A contingency-fee receivables firm for ambulance agencies and ER physician groups that, within 30 days of a self-pay bill, screens the patient for retroactive Medicaid eligibility and files the application for them, turning accounts debt buyers would take at 2-4 cents into full Medicaid payments.
customer: County and municipal EMS agencies, their outsourced ambulance-billing companies, and independent ER, anesthesia and radiology physician groups in Medicaid-expansion states. Rural hospitals under 100 beds are the second wave.
problem: Self-pay accounts sit through 90-180 days of statements before they go to an agency or get sold to a debt buyer, and buyers pay only pennies (a few cents on the dollar for medical accounts). Most states let Medicaid reach back only about 3 months before the application date, so by the time a normal collections workflow gives up, the window in which a real payer could have been found has already closed. Patients get dunned for money they may never have owed, and the provider recovers almost nothing.
solution: Take a nightly feed of new self-pay accounts (demographics only, under a BAA). Screen each one for likely Medicaid or charity-care eligibility. Contact the patient in the first two weeks with a simple offer: we complete your Medicaid application for free. Then file the application, chase documents and caseworkers, and bill Medicaid retroactively for the provider. Patients who do not qualify are routed to charity care or a payment plan, and nobody is ever dunned. The firm is paid a contingency on Medicaid dollars actually collected. The dashboard shows each account's days left in the retro window, so providers see the clock that traditional collections ignore.
why_now: The 2025 budget law (OBBBA) cuts Medicaid retroactive coverage to 1 month for expansion adults and 2 months for everyone else, for applications from January 2027. From then on every day of delay burns covered dates, so speed to application becomes the whole product. Providers are also under revenue pressure, states keep passing medical-debt limits that make selling accounts harder, and Medicaid redetermination and work-requirement churn in 2027 makes eligibility-navigation skills scarce and valuable.
revenue_model: 15-20% contingency on Medicaid reimbursements recovered, with an optional $1-2k/month platform fee for charity-care and medical-debt compliance reporting. Ambulance and physician-group accounts are small ($800-$2,500 each) but high in volume and nearly free to service once the screening flow is built.
non_obvious_insight: Collections looks like a persuasion business but is really a timing business. Every step of the traditional workflow (statements, calls, placement at day 120 or later) pushes action past the point where a third-party payer can still be found. Run the workflow backwards, find the payer inside 30 days, and you get the rare collections company that patients thank you for and that pays the provider 10-30x what a debt buyer would.
first_30_days: Pick one expansion state with a 3-month retro window. Hire two ex-hospital eligibility reps and one engineer. Offer 3 county EMS agencies or their billing companies a free back-test of the last 12 months of self-pay accounts, showing how many were eligible and inside a window where enrollment would have paid. Convert the best result into a contingency pilot on new accounts, ideally with an existing certified navigator status. First Medicaid approvals typically land 45-90 days after filing, so signed pilots come in month 1 and cash in months 3-4.
